evidence: Paths: instruction.md:11 names /instructions/hireops_rules.md and /instructions/integration.md; instruction.md:15 names /assets/seed_data.json. All three exist under task/environment/, and environment/Dockerfile:14-16 does 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/' and chmod -R a+rX (identical to the template). seed_data.json parses (28549 bytes). The solution's copy task/solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical (both SHA256 a1c65c806b54da99a37ab2b5f455ede0a9385a09569903fb3a7f3446f7e83740) and db.js:10 reads it relative to __dirname, as hireops_rules.md section 8 asks, with solve.sh:35 copying solution/app into /app. Content vs brief/rules: users = exactly the 10 accounts and roles in instruction.md:19 and app_context.md:10-19 (3 recruiters, 3 hiring_manager, 1 observer, 3 candidates); no password in the seed, which matches the brief's single shared password that db.js:63 applies. Keys match instruction.md:17 (people, jobs, applications, messages, notes, read markers) and rules section 9 (three jobs; one long conversation, APP-101, 120 messages; 3 notes; 6 read markers; candidate_status_labels matches the table in rules section 7 exactly; thread_page_size 30 matches section 6). Stages are APPLIED..REJECTED in the rules order. Interview counts are within limits (PLAT 2/3, DATA 1/2, DSGN 1/3). Positions within each stage are contiguous from 1. The rejected card APP-301 carries rejected_from SCREEN plus a reason. Every referenced id resolves. Note authors follow the role rules (APP-101 note by USR-MGR1, PLAT's manager; APP-301 note by USR-MGR3, DSGN's manager). Message senders are the job's recruiter or the candidate. Timestamps are sorted and unique within each thread. Every read_count is at most the thread length. generated_note points to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, which exists. Content vs judges: every seeded fact the criteria quote matches the asset. (1) functional prompt.md:33 Z and the hro_unread_counts criterion say Lena starts with 1 unread: APP-301 has 3 messages, Lena's read_count is 2, and message 3 is from USR-REC3 (someone else), so 1 unread. (2) prompt.md:33 and hro_restart give the PLAT order Applied Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi and Screen Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz: matches positions 1-3 and 1-2. Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' matches the APP-101 note verbatim. (3) hro_candidate_view and prompt.md K: Noor Platform Engineer (Infrastructure, INTERVIEW -> Interviewing), Noor Product Designer (Design, APPLIED -> Application received) and Tomas Data Analyst (Finance Systems, SCREEN -> In review) all match. (4) app_context.md:29-30 says Noor's Platform Engineer conversation has 120 messages, which matches APP-101 = 120. hro_thread_latest and hro_thread_earlier then work out to four pages of 30. Rafael's read marker of 120 puts him at the newest message, which the scrolled-up and draft legs need. (5) The gates and the visual/polish 'seeded Data Analyst job' exists (JOB-DATA). Cross-dimension isolation of seed-dependent readings holds: polish prompt.md:24 says 'Never use Lena Fischer's conversation'; visual is read-only; the gates and backend checks only add cards to Data Analyst, never to Platform Engineer. The template seed is a 'CHANGE_ME' placeholder, so the task supplying its own seed is expected. Supporting raw evidence (not run by me): the indexed workspace.cjs (hash verified) asserts the seeded Screen order, Noor's note (lines 54-55), Lena's 1-unread badge (line 486) and the 120-message thread (#061-#120 latest page, line 417) against the golden. This is a scripted golden observation, not a judge run. Lessons check: the seed has no public internet address (no 'http' in seed_data.json, lesson 13). No seed-only hidden demand: every seed-derived fact a judge relies on is either in the public seed and rules or read relative to before-values (lesson 1). Counterexample probes: (a) a broken app that ignores read markers would show Lena 3 or 0 and fail hro_unread_counts. An app that ignores notes or position fails hro_restart. An app that hard-codes a static seed in the browser is excluded by the gates' independent-context add-and-readback. (b) A conforming alternative that maps uppercase stage keys to title-case labels, or stores read markers as message ids instead of counts, still produces the quoted values. The rules define read_count unambiguously ('how many messages ... counted from its first'), so I found no correct reading of the asset that a criterion would fail.
